title: Website Projects
summary: Front-end web projects for CS 1430 using plain HTML, CSS, JS, and Bootstrap

data.text: A collection of 13 front-end web projects built for CS 1430 (Web Fundamentals) at SLCC across 50 commits (May–Aug 2023), progressing from raw HTML pages through CSS layout techniques and Bootstrap, up to JavaScript-driven interactive applications with API integration and game logic, culminating in a Bootstrap portfolio site that ties the entire course together. Each project targets a specific skill set, and the commit history traces a full arc from static markup to dynamic client-side programming — including real learning moments like refactoring bitmask logic per instructor feedback, migrating from local data files to live APIs, and iterating through nine rounds of CSS adjustments to get a pixel-perfect layout right.

items.content: Pure HTML multi-page site — the very first project (commit 1, May 28 2023), a 4-page pizza restaurant skeleton (Home, Contact, About, Order) with no CSS, built entirely with semantic HTML elements
Navigation practice: unordered list <ul>/<li> nav menu linking all four pages, establishing the multi-page structure later expanded into the midterm
Contact form: form with labeled text inputs, email field, textarea, and submit/reset buttons posting to an external PHP endpoint — first exposure to HTML form elements and server-side submission
Pure HTML table with <thead>/<tbody> structure, displaying 9 video entries with name, description, duration, and thumbnail columns
Embedded media: YouTube <iframe> embed below the table for inline video playback
External links: each video title is a clickable <a> linking to YouTube, with inline-styled thumbnail images

data.text: Superheroes — DC vs Marvel Flexbox Layout

items.content: Flexbox two-column layout with justify-content: space-around placing DC Comics and Marvel Comics sections side by side
CSS typography trick: Marvel header uses writing-mode: vertical-rl with transform: scale(-1, -1) for a vertical title rotated to read top-to-bottom
Mixed styling approach: combines internal <style> block (6 properties) with an external stylesheet for separation of concerns practice
Pure CSS illustration of the Kirby character built entirely from <div> elements — no images, only CSS shapes for body, eyes, mouth, blush, hands, legs, and hair tie
Advanced CSS properties: uses border-radius for organic shapes, layered z-index positioning, and geometric background elements (triangle-circle pattern) for the backdrop
Iterative refinement: evolved across multiple commits with responsive adjustments — the commit history shows dedicated passes for box sizing, responsive breakpoints, and layout tweaks
Horizontal navigation bar using styled <ul>/<li> elements with CSS for inline layout across a 4-page site (Home, Contact, About, Order)
HTML form handling: contact page with labeled input fields (<input>, <textarea>) posting to an external PHP endpoint for server-side processing

4-page responsive site (Home, Contact, About, Order) for a fictional pizza restaurant with consistent navigation and custom CSS across all pages — the largest single commit in the course (15 commits total including the initial batch, CSS ordering optimizations, and subsequent refinements)

Complex order form: 8 icon-labeled checkbox toppings (pepperoni, sausage, ham, meatballs, red onion, jalapeno, mushroom, broccoli), radio button size selector, crust dropdown (<select>), and a full delivery information section with text, email, tel, and textarea inputs
Form features: HTML5 validation with required attributes, a 50-state <select> dropdown, and separate reset/submit buttons posting to an external PHP endpoint

Semantic HTML refactoring: a dedicated commit replaced <section> tags with <header> in header sections across all four pages, plus a separate commit aligned input and select element heights for consistent form styling
Visual design: custom background images per page via header IDs, decorative arrow and icon graphics, and a two-column card layout for the order page
Pixel-perfect CSS recreation of the Wordle game interface — static layout, no JavaScript — replicating the 5×6 letter grid and 3-row on-screen keyboard
CSS Grid layout: the letter grid uses a grid-wrapper with 30 cells (6 rows × 5 columns), and the keyboard uses nested <div> rows matching the QWERTY layout including an ENTER key and delete icon
Header bar: nav icon, centered title, and right-aligned icon group (help, statistics, settings) — all positioned with CSS to match the original Wordle UI

Iterative polish: 9 commits spanning initial layout, icon image uploads, detailed HTML comments, and three separate rounds of size adjustments — including a typo fix that was committed and then reverted, showing real version control learning
Bootstrap rebuild of the Crusty Bite Pizza site — same multi-page structure reimplemented using Bootstrap 5 components instead of custom CSS
Responsive navbar: navbar-expand-md with a collapsible hamburger toggler (navbar-toggler) for mobile, dark theme (bg-dark navbar-dark), and right-aligned nav links
Bootstrap utilities: container system, margin/text utility classes (mt-4, text-center), and bootstrap.bundle.min.js for interactive components
Cascading prompt inputs with validation — collects name (rejects empty), age (rejects NaN and negatives via parseInt + charAt check), and birth month (accepts both full name and number)

Data lookups: month-to-number mapping object supporting bidirectional lookup, season calculation by slicing the months array into quarters, and a birthstone dictionary with article (a/an) determination via vowel check on the first character

DOM rendering: dynamically injects a personalized birthday message into the page with a CSS opacity transition fade-in effect on window.onload — a follow-up commit fixed the initial loading state so the fade-in triggers correctly
Prompt-based input validation: accepts an integer 1–7 for the number of lottery pairs, rejecting NaN, non-integers, and out-of-range values in a while loop
Random number generation: produces 1–7 random numbers (1–99) with zero-padding for single digits, formatted as a dash-separated string
CSS animation reset: uses requestAnimationFrame with a nested setTimeout to force-restart a CSS warning animation by toggling animationName between 'none' and ''

WordsAPI integration: validates every user-entered word against the WordsAPI (wordsapiv1.p.rapidapi.com) to confirm it matches the required part of speech (noun, verb, or adjective) before generating the story

Evolved architecture: originally shipped with local adjectives.js and verbs.js word-list files and a local npm pluralize dependency — over 7 commits, migrated the word lists to the Random Words API (random-words-api.vercel.app), switched pluralize from npm to a CDN, and restructured animals.js from a 227-line flat array to a compact data format

Regex-based verb conjugation: a one-liner function converts present-tense verbs to past tense, handling consonant-y→i (carry→carried), consonant doubling (stop→stopped), and silent-e dropping (dance→danced) via chained .replace() calls

Async coordination: uses fetch().then() chains for API calls with a setTimeout gate to wait for all validation promises before generating the story, plus the pluralize library (via CDN) for singular noun handling

data.text: Tic Tac Toe — Bitwise Win Detection

items.content: Bitwise game engine: each cell is assigned a power-of-2 value (1, 2, 4, … 256), and each player's score is the bitwise OR of their occupied cells — win checking uses (score & winCode) === winCode against 8 precomputed bitmasks representing all winning lines

Bitmask revision: the original implementation assigned cell values starting at 2 (2, 4, 8, … 512) with a tie check of 1022 — a dedicated commit per instructor feedback corrected the encoding to start at 1 (1, 2, 4, … 256) with all 8 winCode values recalculated and the tie check updated to 511 (2⁹ − 1)
Dynamic board generation: builds the 3×3 grid programmatically with nested loops, assigning each cell's bit value via onclick handlers injected through innerHTML

Game features: two-player mode with custom player names, persistent scoreboard tracking wins and ties across rounds, sound effects for win and tie events, and a "Play Again" button that resets the board while preserving scores

Bootstrap + MDB portfolio page (252-line HTML, 234-line CSS) tying all 11 course projects together — the single largest commit in the repo (862 insertions) followed by 8 iterative refinement commits for layout and styling adjustments
Multi-item Bootstrap carousel: project screenshot gallery using carousel-item elements with a JS loop that clones sibling slides to display 3 cards at a time, with smooth sliding transitions
Dynamic quote system: fetches from a local quotes.json (201 lines of inspirational quotes) and injects a random quote into a <blockquote> element with a clickable refresh icon

Bootstrap components: responsive navbar-expand-md with dropdown project menu featuring color-coded skill badges (HTML, HTML+CSS, Bootstrap, JavaScript), scrollspy-tracked sections, and an offcanvas panel for an embedded Spotify audio player
Project screenshots: 12 PNG images captured and organized for the carousel, with direct links to each project folder — the portfolio page serves as both a course showcase and a navigation hub

CSS-only character illustration: Building the Kirby figure from pure CSS required computing exact border-radius percentages, layering z-index values for overlapping shapes (eyes over face, blush over head), and using pseudo-elements for decorative details — no images allowed, so every curve is a styled div.

Wordle grid precision: Replicating the Wordle UI demanded precise CSS Grid sizing for the 5×6 letter grid and three keyboard rows with unequal key widths (ENTER and DELETE wider than letter keys), all matching the original spacing and proportions without JavaScript — refined across 9 commits including three separate size adjustment passes.

Local-to-API migration: Mad Libs originally bundled local adjectives.js and verbs.js word-list files with a local npm dependency. Over several commits, the architecture shifted to fetching random words from a live API and loading the pluralize library via CDN — requiring changes to async flow, dependency management, and the "I'm Feeling Lucky" random-fill logic.

Bitmask encoding correction: The original Tic Tac Toe assigned cell values starting at 2 instead of 1, making all 8 win-code bitmasks and the tie-check value wrong. A dedicated commit per instructor feedback recalculated every value — e.g., top row changed from 14 to 7, tie check from 1022 to 511 — a lesson in how one off-by-one in a bit scheme cascades through the entire game logic.

Regex verb conjugation edge cases: The past-tense converter needed to handle irregular English patterns — consonant+y endings (carry→carried), short vowel consonant doubling (stop→stopped), and silent-e words (dance→danced) — all in a single chained regex function.

Git workflow learning curve: Early commits show a real .gitignore struggle — 4 consecutive commits toggling between adding and clearing cached files from tracking, learning how .gitignore only prevents future tracking and doesn't remove already-tracked files without git rm --cached.
Languages: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6)
Frameworks: Bootstrap 5 (navbar, grid system, responsive utilities, collapse, dropdown, carousel, scrollspy, offcanvas), MDB (Material Design for Bootstrap)
Layout Techniques: Flexbox, CSS Grid, float-based positioning, writing-mode transforms, border-radius shape construction
Forms: HTML5 input types (text, email, tel, radio, checkbox, select, textarea), required validation, form submission to external PHP endpoints

JavaScript Concepts: DOM manipulation (innerHTML, createElement, event handlers), prompt-based input with validation loops, fetch API with async/then chains, regex string processing, bitwise operations for game state, JSON data loading
API Integration: WordsAPI (part-of-speech validation), Random Words API (random word generation), RapidAPI authentication headers, local JSON data fetching
Design: CSS-only illustrations, pixel-perfect UI cloning, responsive navigation, icon-labeled form controls, CSS animations with requestAnimationFrame reset
Version Control: Git workflow across 50 commits — branching from initial scaffolds to iterative refinements, .gitignore management, semantic commit messages, and a revert/re-commit cycle
